text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Bank insurer ING Groep reports 1996 net 25 pct higher at Dfl 33 bn. (p1)
- Dutch economy will get an extra growth impulse in 1998, if EMU proceeds without significant problems according to central planning bureau CPB. (p1)
- ABN Amro bank seeks to change pension system of its 35,000 employees. (p1)
- Automation firm CSS applies for a listing on the Amsterdam stock exchange's new market NMAX exchange. (p3)
- Director of regional public transport company Vancom steps down, because introduction of competition in public transport takes too long. (p3)
- Dutch national debt could drop by some 250 million guilders through the sale of public broadcasters' unit NOB. (p3)
- Department store and services group Vendex sells remainng stake in U.S. bookstore chain Barnes & Noble. (p4)
- Oil and gas company NAM gets permission to test drill in the environmentally sensitive Wadden Sea. (p4)
-VOLKSKRANT
- Central planning bureau CPB wants more focus on employees older than 50 who lose their jobs. (p1)
- Production of the last Fokker 70 puts pressure on talks about relaunching the bankrupt aircraft maker. (p2)
- Technical services group GTI sells its security systems unit GTI Industrial Automation to Japan's Yokogawa. (p2)
- Postal arm of Dutch PTT KPN wins court case against its German rival Deutsche Bundespost over DB's cancellation of large TNT TNT.AX contract. (p15) DE TELEGRAAF
- Environment group for the Wadden Sea prepares new fight against economic ministry's drill permit for the NAM. (p7)
- Pay and conditions talks for Dutch employees of Royal Dutch/Shell grind to a halt. (p25)
- Construction group BAM is expecting at least 20 million guilders profit in 1997 after 1996 losses. (p27)
- Option trader Sem van Berkel is to start cooperation with bank Kempen & Co to set up a new options unit. (p29) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch bourse-listed companies have made an average of Dfl 29,000 profit per employee in 1996. (p1) TROUW
- Losses from the ongoing swine fever epidemic amount to over one billion guilders - CPB. (p1)
- Dutch Mobil filling stations start redecoration operation to adapt to the green colours of its partner BP. (p4)
